text:
alex: Heads-up: I hit a weird streaming bug on mobile Safari + our CDN where two SSE events get coalesced into one payload and browser parser chokes. Go and node SDKs unaffected.
mina: coalesced how? CDN merging chunks into a single TCP frame?
alex: yes, logs from edge show: `chunkA

chunkB` arriving as a single read. Browser EventSource fires one message with data=="chunkA

chunkB" which our sample app tries to parse per event and fails ordering assumptions.
jord: can you paste minimal logs and sample-app snippet?
alex: snippet in samples/mobile-offline-stream: `eventSource.onmessage = e => handleChunk(e.data)` and handleChunk assumes single chunk payload. Logs: ```
[2111-11-11T12:00:01Z] edge: forwarded aggregated read len=512 seq=41 parts=2
[2111-11-11T12:00:01Z] runtime: emit seq=41 data="{\"t\":\"A\"}"
[2111-11-11T12:00:01Z] runtime: keepalive
[2111-11-11T12:00:01Z] runtime: emit seq=42 data="{\"t\":\"B\"}"
[2111-11-11T12:00:02Z] browser: onmessage -> data="{\\\"t\\\":\\\"A\\\"}

{\\\"t\\\":\\\"B\\\"}"
```
mina: ouch. So the SDK parity issue is that low-level libs present events differently. Node's eventsource splits by `\n\n` while browser collapses into one message if the server coalesced frames.
jord: mitigation options: 1) server/runtime: add explicit `event:` lines and `id:` to separate events; 2) client: split incoming `e.data` by `\n\n` and treat multiple JSON blobs inside one event; 3) CDN: disable coalescing (likely hard).
alex: I prototyped option 2 in mobile helper: `for (const part of e.data.split(/\n\n+/)) { try { handle(JSON.parse(part)) } catch(e) { buffer += part } }` worked in my local runs.
mina: careful: splitting on `\n\n` can break if a data block contains blank lines intentionally. Better: runtime add `event: chunk\n` prefix for each chunk so EventSource splits correctly.
jord: longer-term we should standardize the framing: `event: chunk` + `data: {seq,resume,part}`. That way even if CDN merges lines, the EventSource spec still emits separate messages? Actually EventSource splits at \n\n boundaries; but if CDN merges they still remain two events in stream. Browser grouping of reads shouldn't change EventSource event boundaries if server sends `event:` prefixes. Coalescing only affects TCP frames, not SSE framing. Still might be safe to add explicit event names.
alex: created a tiny reproducer and PR in sample-app to defensively split e.data by `}{` boundary too (handles coalesced JSON objects) and fallback to buffer. PR #4755.
mina: please also add a unit that simulates CDN coalesce and mobile Safari behavior. Add note in DX docs about mobile Safari differences and CDNs.
js-bot: CI: ran sample-app tests on PR #4755: 30/30 passes locally; queued browser matrix.
ci-bot: CI: browser matrix: Chrome 60/60, Safari iOS 17 58/60 (2 flakes).
jord: ok short-term land the sample-app defensive parsing + docs. Long-term runtime RFC for explicit `event:` markers and an SDK parity test harness that runs sample-app across go/node/python/mobile browsers.
alex: filed INFRA-333 to log edge coalescing heuristics and ask CDN vendor. Thanks folks :wave:
